Let me trace through the program with this input.

T = 1, so one test case.
N = 1002, K = 1002.

A = [1, 2, 3, ..., 1002]
B = [1, 2, 3, ..., 1001, 1]

So B is the same as A except the last element: A ends with 1002, B ends with 1.

First check: `if A == B:` — they are not equal (A[1001] = 1002, B[1001] = 1). So no.

Then check all b in B are in set(A). B contains 1..1001 and 1, all of which are in A (1..1002). So judge remains True.

K = 1002 > 1, so we go into the elif K > 1 branch.

sB = set(B) = {1, ..., 1001}, len(sB) = 1001. len(B) = 1002. So len(sB) != len(B), so we don't print 'No'. We go into the else:

judge = False
kakunin = {}
for n in range(N):
    if B[n] not in kakunin:
        kakunin[B[n]] = [n]
    else:
        if kakunin[B[n]][-1] >= n - K:
            judge = True
        kakunin[B[n]].append(n)

B[1001] = 1, which was first seen at n=0. kakunin[1][-1] = 0. Check: 0 >= 1001 - 1002 = -1. Yes, 0 >= -1 is True. So judge = True.

Then print('Yes').

So the output is "Yes".
